neighbours.label: position or timing references on rotating machinery: timing marks, a shaft or piston reaching an index position, alignment of sprockets and gears
fire: With the cover off, make sure the timing marks on the camshaft gear and the block are lined up.
Rotate the flywheel slowly until the piston in cylinder one reaches top dead centre.
A sensor produces one pulse each time the notch on the shaft passes the pickup.
Set the distributor so the rotor points at the mark for the first cylinder.
Turn the pulley clockwise until the groove lines up with the zero on the timing scale.
The encoder disc has a single index slot that marks one full revolution of the spindle.
Before fitting the chain, align the dot on the sprocket with the arrow on the housing.
As the cam turns, the follower reaches its highest point once per revolution.
quiet: With the cover off, make sure the gasket on the camshaft housing is clean and dry.
Drain the coolant slowly until the radiator in the front is completely empty.
A sensor produces a warning each time the temperature of the oil gets too high.
Clean the distributor cap so the contacts are free of dust and grease.
Tighten the bolts evenly until the cover sits flat against the engine block.
The brake disc has a thin rust layer that comes off after a short drive.
Before fitting the tyre, inspect the rim for dents and remove the old weights.
As the engine warms, the fan switches on to keep the coolant from boiling.

notes: Top examples: timing chain, marker, notch, 'mark a line', rotary encoder, step pulse, 'turn the engine over'. Probes: timing marks 2.47 and 1.26 (above the corpus max), shaft passing the index position 1.78, piston reaching the top 0.66, but also a crankshaft sentence with no mark 0.92 and a teacher's 'mark' 0.41; oil change 0.02. Near misses are car-maintenance sentences with no rotation-position reference.
